name: Northern Ndebele
notes: Northern Ndebele (isiNdebele, Zimbabwe) — Nguni Bantu language, Guthrie S.44, close relative of Zulu. Shares Zulu's three click series — dental (c/ǀ), alveolar (q/ǃ), lateral (x/ǁ) — each with plain, aspirated, and voiced (prenasalized/depressor) variants, plus ejective affricates tj /tʃʼ/, ts /tsʼ/, and kl /kxʼ/ (a velar, not lateral, ejective affricate) not present in standard Zulu. ⟨dl⟩ is the voiced lateral fricative /ɮ/ and ⟨hl⟩ the voiceless lateral fricative /ɬ/ (not affricates). Prenasalized consonants (mb, nd, ng, nj, nz…) are single phonemes. Five-vowel system a/e/i/o/u; mid vowels e, o each have open [ɛ, ɔ] and close [e, o] realizations (Wikipedia, Northern Ndebele language). Like other Nguni languages Northern Ndebele is a tone language, but tone is not marked in the standard orthography.

sources.author: Sibanda, Galen
sources.title: Verbal Phonology and Morphology of Ndebele
sources.publisher: University of California, Berkeley PhD dissertation (eScholarship)
sources.notes: Chapter 1 inventory tables (3a-3c) and the word lists (4)-(6) on pp. 4-7, read on the page image (the eScholarship scan has no text layer). Table 3b gives the three click places (dental ⟨c⟩, post-alveolar ⟨q⟩, alveolar lateral ⟨x⟩) in five series each: plain, aspirated ⟨ch qh xh⟩, voiced depressor ⟨gc gq gx⟩, voiced nasalised ⟨nc nq nx⟩ and voiced nasalised depressor ⟨ngc ngq ngx⟩. Table 3c gives the affricates: ⟨j⟩ = dʒ, ⟨tsh⟩ = both tʃʰ and the ejective tʃʼ (spelled alike), ⟨ts⟩ = tsʼ, ⟨kl⟩ = kx, prenasalised ⟨nts ntsh nkl⟩. Against this map: the depressor nasal clicks ⟨ngc ngq ngx⟩ have no key; the map's ⟨tj tjh⟩ keys are not in Sibanda's spelling, where the palatal affricates are both ⟨tsh⟩; and ⟨kl⟩ is given as kx rather than kxʼ. He also notes the velar ⟨k⟩ is a weakly voiced fricative [ɣ] in the non-depressor series. Recorded here, not changed.

ancestors.notes: Nguni branch of Bantu, within Atlantic-Congo.
Closely related Nguni sister language; Northern Ndebele derives historically from a 19th-century Zulu-speaking migration into Zimbabwe.
Khoisan substrate: source of the click consonants (c, q, x series).

location.notes: Approximate centre of the Northern Ndebele speaking area, Matabeleland, Zimbabwe.
